floor_history.headline: recon: floor=2 is pure sched1 lbu-emission-order swap in FALSE-color branch; regs+opcodes identical, only [b,r,g] vs [r,g,b]; statement-reorder KILLED
s2 structural: struct-cast, walking-pointer, ternary-hoist, block-local-split all KILLED at floor=2; two-block lbu structure is load-bearing (cannot consolidate)

frontier.hypothesis: Add a use of `b` between its load and the OR-chain that combine/CSE cannot fold away, extending b's INSN_PRIORITY chain length to >=4 without changing final bytes.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 priority = longest reverse chain to end-of-block; a real (non-DCE-able) intermediate consumer of b bumps its chain length, tying with or exceeding r/g.
frontier.next_probe: Any concrete C shape that survives combine without being DCE'd AND leaves the emitted 7-insn FALSE block bytes intact is expected to be either (a) impossible-by-construction (the extra chain link would show as an extra insn), or (b) cheat-shaped (side-effect-free op inserted for codegen only). Enumerate to prove dead.

frontier.hypothesis: The original C was written such that TRUE and FALSE arms share NO code from `b/r/g` upward — perhaps the FALSE arm was written as a helper function inlined by hand: e.g., `gnd_load_tex(pack_bgr(player))` where pack_bgr is defined inline right above and takes player, loading through a distinct pointer local.
frontier.mechanism: A distinct pointer local materialized fresh (not aliased with `p`/`q` from the loops earlier) may cause GCC's alias-tracking / register-renumbering to give the three lbu's different pseudos with priority order matching target.
frontier.next_probe: Try `u8 *cp = (u8*)player; b=cp[0x1A]; r=cp[0x18]; g=cp[0x19];` with cp declared fresh in the block. Note: this is one axis away from the walking-pointer that was KILLED; the difference is `cp` is not derived arithmetically from the target address. Predict same fold-collapse but measure. If still 2, try declaring cp OUTSIDE the else block (function scope) so its liveness spans the whole tail.

frontier.hypothesis: The FALSE arm was originally written with an inline helper like `PACK_RGB(b,r,g)` macro that expanded to a different RTL sequence (e.g., using a temp local for one of the sub-ORs), so that the intermediate variable's def-use extended a chain onto b.
frontier.mechanism: Explicit named intermediate lifts one sub-computation's LUID/pseudo lifetime and reshuffles sched1 without touching final register assignment.
frontier.next_probe: Try `s32 rg = (r<<16) | (g<<8); gnd_load_tex(b | rg);` -- introduces a named intermediate for the r,g sub-tree. Does NOT change parenthesization (still `b | (rg)`), does NOT dead-store (rg is used), stays outside or-tree-shape-shift ban. Predict this may re-schedule if sched1 sees rg's def as a separate BB or a live-out. Sandbox and measure.
